body.title: Living Looms: Silk Brocade, Hand-Block Wood and Sungudi Knot-Dye Guilds
body.summary: Comparing the master guild structures, natural mordants, and oral transmission systems of Banaras, Sanganer, and Madurai.

rationale.text: All three traditions depend on close-knit artisanal communities (Julahas/Ansaris in Varanasi, Chhipas in Rajasthan, Saurashtrians in Madurai) who preserved complex chemical and tactile knowledge through family lineages.

whyItMatters.text: India's surviving handloom diversity is unique globally; these artisanal guilds constitute a living repository of sustainable craft and community self-reliance.

body.doesNotEstablish: This comparative lineage does not claim historical migration between the three specific craft communities, but examines their parallel guild preservation models under royal and temple patronage.
body.uncertainty: Pre-colonial guild regulations were preserved through oral lineage contracts and master-disciple oaths rather than state registry archives.

claims.text: Distinct artisanal communities passed down specialized textile knowledge through family workshops.

evidence.excerpt: Weaving techniques and motif drawing were transmitted orally across master-apprentice and father-son lines in guild workshops.

claims.text: Geographical Indication protections help sustain artisanal handloom economies against factory imitation.

evidence.excerpt: GI registration protects the authentic handloom heritage and guarantees consumer traceability.
